title: Redox Reactions
seo_title: Redox Reactions Class 11 Chemistry Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 7)
standard_text: Concept of oxidation and reduction, redox reactions, oxidation number, balancing redox reactions in terms of loss and gain of electrons and change in oxidation number, applications of redox reactions.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 11 Chemistry worksheets for NCERT Chapter 7 Redox Reactions: oxidation and reduction, oxidation numbers, oxidising and reducing agents, half-equations and disproportionation. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Oxidation is loss of electrons; reduction is gain (OIL RIG).
key_sub: The oxidising agent is itself reduced.
body_html:
How to think about it

Oxidation is the loss of electrons, or an increase in oxidation number; reduction is the gain of electrons, or a decrease. They always happen together. The oxidising agent takes electrons and is reduced; the reducing agent gives electrons and is oxidised.

Oxidation numbers follow rules: elements are 0, oxygen is usually −2 (−1 in peroxides), hydrogen +1 (−1 in metal hydrides), and the sum equals the charge. Redox equations are balanced by electrons in half-equations. In disproportionation one element is both oxidised and reduced.

Example

Oxidation number of Mn in KMnO₄?

+1 + x − 8 = 0

Answer: +7

Example

Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu. Reducing agent?

Zn loses electrons

Answer: Zn

Common mistakes

  • Calling the substance that is oxidised the oxidising agent.
  • Taking O as −2 in H₂O₂.
  • Forgetting that the sum in an ion equals the charge.

faq.q: How do you find an oxidation number?
faq.a: Use the rules (O is −2, H is +1, the sum equals the charge) and solve for the unknown element.

items.q: Is this change oxidation or reduction: H₂O₂ → 2H₂O (in acid)?
items.e: H₂O₂ + 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → 2H₂O. Electrons on the left mean reduction (gain); on the right mean oxidation (loss).
